meta.purpose: Menu of literature-grounded behaviors used by the emergence verifier (program/harness.md §5.5). A formalism earns credit for behaviors that emerge from its core premises, not for ones written into it.

kind_legend.non-phenomenon: Negative control: a behavior the literature reports does NOT occur. The system should exclude it

verdict_legend.emergent: Derivable from core premises with no premise specific to this phenomenon
verdict_legend.parametric: Emergent within a parameter regime that is motivated independently of this phenomenon (state it in notes)
verdict_legend.postulated: The phenomenon is, or is equivalent to, a core premise. Consistent, but earns no emergence credit
verdict_legend.bolted-on: Needs an assumption added for this phenomenon (listed in extra_assumptions)
verdict_legend.contradicted: The formalism predicts the opposite: a falsification flag
verdict_legend.excluded: For non-phenomena only: the formalism rules the behavior out (the desired outcome)
verdict_legend.generated: For non-phenomena only: the formalism produces the behavior (a false positive)

derivation_status_legend.proved: Derivation at verification tier V4 or above, or a published theorem

strength_legend.robust: Many independent replications or a textbook law
strength_legend.theorized-only: Theorized in its field, not yet observed empirically: a prediction target

pattern_legend.theorized-then-observed: The Firth pattern: theory preceded the empirical confirmation
pattern_legend.theorized-only: Awaiting observation; LLMs may supply the apparatus (debates.json)

formalisms.description: This program: GM primitives A1–A14, spine L0–L8, outline v1. Core premises are GM-A1..GM-A14.
Transmission as noisy replication (memetics; Shannon channel without selection or context).
Griffiths & Kalish: chains of Bayesian learners converge to the prior.
Sperber: reconstructive transmission toward cognitive attractors.
Boyd & Richerson / Cavalli-Sforza: population-genetic models of cultural evolution with biases.

meta.scoring: See program/tools/phenomena.py and harness.md §5.5. Weights are initial and should be recalibrated.

phenomena.behavior: Words that occur in similar contexts have similar meanings: distributional similarity tracks semantic similarity.
phenomena.operationalization: In the cyclic world, embeddings fit to co-occurrence recover the orbit geometry of the world states they refer to.

assessments.notes: Close to postulated: A14 says reference induces co-occurrence. Credit depends on A14 being motivated independently of Firth (it is: by reference, not by meaning). The geometry step (S5) is published.

phenomena.behavior: Representations of cyclic or spatial word families (months, colors, places, sky positions) reproduce the world's geometry.
phenomena.operationalization: Fourier/irrep structure of family Gram matrices; per-irrep radii.

assessments.notes: S5 is a published theorem (Storan; Karkada) once S1's invariance holds.

phenomena.behavior: Law of conformity: frequent words change meaning more slowly.

source_hints: Hamilton, Leskovec & Jurafsky (2016), Diachronic word embeddings reveal statistical laws of semantic change, ACL — not in bibliography; verify

phenomena.operationalization: Per-word drift rate across generations versus family-relevant token mass n_eff.

assessments.notes: Candidate mechanism: estimation error and drift scale with 1/n_eff. Same mechanism as P-004; one mechanism for two phenomena is a good sign if it holds.

phenomena.behavior: Irregular verbs regularize, and rare ones regularize faster (rate roughly inverse square root of frequency).

source_hints: Lieberman, Michel, Jackson, Tang & Nowak (2007), Quantifying the evolutionary dynamics of language, Nature — not in bibliography; verify

phenomena.operationalization: Irregular forms as low-mass exceptions (world-type B-perp) under the generational map; survival time versus frequency.

assessments.notes: The exponent is a sharp target: the system must produce a frequency^-1/2 law without tuning, or this is bolted-on.

phenomena.behavior: Word frequencies follow Zipf's law.

source_hints: Zipf (1949); Piantadosi (2014), Zipf's word frequency law in natural language: a critical review, Psychonomic Bulletin & Review — verify

phenomena.operationalization: Rank-frequency distribution of tokens generated by agents in the system.

assessments.notes: Nothing in the spine generates frequency distributions. Recorded to expose the gap.

phenomena.behavior: Languages change, yet texts remain translatable across languages and eras.
phenomena.operationalization: Family geometries across languages align up to a gauge; world symmetry breaking pins the gauge (OUT-X13).

assessments.notes: A GM test case, so it informed the design.

phenomena.behavior: Under iterated learning, languages become more structured and easier to learn.
phenomena.operationalization: Chains of Bayesian learners in the toy world: compressibility of the transmitted code across generations.

assessments.notes: K32 imports the Griffiths–Kalish result. Under the 'prior replaces evidence' mechanism, structure emerges toward the learners' prior.

phenomena.behavior: Serial reproduction regresses toward the transmitters' cultural schemas.

source_hints: Bartlett (1932), Remembering — not in bibliography; verify

phenomena.operationalization: Closed transmission chain without independent evidence: the distribution of readings converges to the reader prior.

assessments.notes: The drift term of T3 is exactly this. The convergence result is published (Griffiths & Kalish).

phenomena.behavior: Smaller or isolated populations lose cultural complexity (the Tasmanian case).
phenomena.operationalization: Fidelity threshold versus effective population of sources.

assessments.notes: A11 is taken from Henrich, so this earns no emergence credit. Contested by vaesen2016.

phenomena.behavior: Pure social learning does not raise mean fitness in a changing environment (Rogers' paradox); critical or individual learning resolves it.
phenomena.operationalization: Population with copiers and testers under a drifting world; mean grounded information.

assessments.notes: Info-theoretic core proved in proofs/psitip (T2; T4.2 corrected): a closed loop cannot gain. The threshold v* (K33) is still a conjecture.

phenomena.behavior: Cumulative culture (the ratchet) requires high-fidelity transmission.

assessments.notes: This is axiom A11.

phenomena.behavior: Conformist and prestige biases shape which variants spread.

extra_assumptions: drift is defined as retention 'for reasons unrelated to the world', which lists these biases
assessments.notes: The spine sorts these biases into the drift term but does not predict their form or strength. Accommodated, not derived.

phenomena.behavior: Content biases: negative, threat-related and social information survives transmission chains better.

source_hints: Mesoudi, Whiten & Dunbar (2006), British Journal of Psychology; Bebbington et al. (2017) — verify

assessments.notes: No mechanism ties the content of a reading to its retention probability. A candidate extension is relevance weights w(kappa), as in S17.

phenomena.behavior: Transmission is reconstructive: variants converge to attractors rather than replicating faithfully (cultural attraction).
phenomena.operationalization: Fixed points of the generational map under reader priors.

assessments.notes: Attractors are the modes of the prior. Parametric because which attractors appear depends on the prior.

phenomena.behavior: Social influence breaks the wisdom of crowds: it raises inequality and unpredictability of success.
phenomena.operationalization: Aggregation accuracy versus effective number of independent sources A_eff.

assessments.notes: Correlated evidence lowers A_eff. That gives accuracy loss, but the inequality of success needs the attachment dynamics of K28.

phenomena.behavior: Information cascades: agents rationally ignore private signals and herd.

assessments.notes: K37 is a known result, re-applied.

phenomena.behavior: Oral traditions transmit through formulas and themes rather than verbatim text.
phenomena.operationalization: Under copy noise, codes with redundant, formulaic units survive longer: the redundancy term in T6.

assessments.notes: A12 postulates the oral/literate split. The formula-as-error-correction step is what would earn the credit.

phenomena.behavior: Print increases textual fixity and standardization.

assessments.notes: Media regimes are points in (c, phi, n). Fixity follows from higher copy fidelity phi.

phenomena.behavior: Literary frame: a canonical work cannot be paraphrased without loss (the heresy of paraphrase); fidelity norms approach strict equality.

source_hints: Brooks (1947), The Well Wrought Urn — not in bibliography; verify

phenomena.operationalization: Paraphrase loss versus K(work | reader model); context-truncation degradation (GM C18, C19).

assessments.notes: Must come out of the same mechanism as P-031 with only the frame varied. Two mechanisms would count as a bolt-on.

phenomena.behavior: Pulp/genre frame: texts tolerate heavy compression, skimming, abridgment and dropped passages with little loss of what readers value.
phenomena.operationalization: Information concentrated in the genre prior: reading still succeeds with ablated attention or dropped packets (GM C19).

assessments.notes: The contrast pair is the test: one compressibility-relative-to-prior mechanism, with the frame setting the distortion measure.

phenomena.behavior: Creative misprision: strong misreadings of predecessors drive literary innovation.
phenomena.operationalization: In the selection simulation, some misreadings raise grounded information or value under testing (pool + select > drift).

assessments.notes: T1 (misprision is unavoidable) is the easy part. The creative branch needs T3's threshold, which is a conjecture. If it fails to emerge, the formalism is wrong (per program design).

phenomena.behavior: Reception is historical: a work's meaning and value shift with the readers' horizon of expectations.

assessments.notes: A6 (re-reading in changed contexts) is close to the phenomenon itself, so this risks being postulated.

phenomena.behavior: Most works are lost; survival of medieval literature is heavily skewed and incomplete.
phenomena.operationalization: Unseen-species estimate of loss in the archive model versus copy rate.

phenomena.behavior: Sleeping beauties: some works are neglected for a long time, then suddenly recognized.
Cumulative advantage: attention, citations and canonical status concentrate (the Matthew effect).

assessments.notes: Unclear whether preferential attachment is derived or assumed in the canon-network layer. Assess.

phenomena.behavior: Some works are reread for millennia without being exhausted (Homer is still read).

source_hints: A Homeric reception history covering the commentary tradition from the Alexandrian scholia to the present — source to be chosen and verified

assessments.notes: A GM test case.

phenomena.behavior: Interpretive communities: commentary splits into camps that read the same text differently.
Defamiliarization: art works by making the familiar strange; novelty followed by resonance marks influential texts.
Indeterminacy of translation: evidence underdetermines reference.

assessments.notes: It is an identifiability class: geometry is fixed up to a gauge (Roeder; Marconato).

phenomena.behavior: Form alone cannot ground meaning (the symbol-grounding problem; the octopus test).
phenomena.operationalization: Meaning from form is possible as a state (a snapshot) and impossible as a process (no refresh without independent evidence).

assessments.notes: The 'impossible as process' half is proved in proofs/psitip. The 'possible as state' half rests on T8 / S1.

phenomena.behavior: Testimony transmits knowledge, but only under vigilance; vigilance fails against coherent consensus error.

assessments.notes: The first half is postulated by A5. The emergent part is K34's claim that vigilance checks the prior, not the world.

phenomena.behavior: Illusion of explanatory depth: people believe they understand mechanisms far better than they do.

assessments.notes: Possible link: explicit content (what can be run) versus held but unrun instructions. Not assessed.

phenomena.behavior: Psychosis as aberrant precision weighting of prediction errors.
Model collapse: recursive training on generated data loses distribution tails first.
phenomena.operationalization: Per-irrep radii and B-perp_world across self-training generations (OUT-X7, X14).

assessments.notes: 'No gain' is proved (T2). 'Tails first' rests on the S22 shrinkage mechanism, a conjecture.

phenomena.behavior: Accumulating real data alongside synthetic data prevents collapse; replacing it does not.

assessments.notes: T4 says accumulation stops the loss but cannot produce gain.

phenomena.behavior: Representations of different models converge as scale grows (the Platonic Representation Hypothesis).

assessments.notes: Emergent on symmetric families. The program also predicts that convergence is not grounding (S25, S26; S26 is proved).

phenomena.behavior: LLM outputs are homogeneous across models and users (an 'artificial hivemind'); AI assistance reduces collective diversity.
Sycophancy: models trained on human approval tell users what they want to hear.
NON-PHENOMENON: closed-loop retelling chains steadily increase accuracy about the world.

assessments.notes: Excluded by T2 (proofs/psitip row 1).

phenomena.behavior: NON-PHENOMENON: agreement between models always implies agreement with the world.

assessments.notes: Excluded with a counterexample: proofs/psitip row 9 (shared data).

phenomena.behavior: NON-PHENOMENON: every misreading is degradation; there is no creative branch.

assessments.notes: Excluded if T3's select term is positive. Depends on the λ* conjecture.

phenomena.behavior: NON-PHENOMENON: literary and genre texts lose the same amount under paraphrase or compression.
NON-PHENOMENON: embedding geometry is arbitrary and unrelated to the structure of the referents.
